chunks: Saad ibn Abdullah narrated from Abu Hashim al-Ja'fari who said: I was imprisoned with Abu Muhammad (peace be upon him) in the prison of al-Muhtadi ibn al-Wathiq.

He said to me: O Abu Hashim, this transgressor wanted to play with divine destiny in this night, and Allah has cut off his life and made it for the Qa'im after him. I did not have a son, but I will be granted a son. Abu Hashim said: When we woke up in the morning, the Turks attacked al-Muhtadi and killed him, and al-Mu'tamid succeeded him, and Allah saved us.
ai.seo_question: What did Imam Hasan al-Askari (a.s.) predict about Caliph al-Muhtadi and his own offspring?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* records Imam Hasan al-Askari (a.s.) predicting the sudden death of Caliph al-Muhtadi by the Turks and the rise of al-Mu'tamid, while also foretelling the birth of his son, the Mahdi, to a childless father. It underscores the divine decree (*hukm Allah*) over political powers, illustrating how the Imam’s knowledge of unseen events confirms his authority during the Minor Exile. The event serves as a key proof for the continuity of the Imamate and the imminent appearance of the Twelfth Imam.
